title: Doubly efficient PIR with quasilinear server preprocessing
formal: Under the specified Ring-LWE assumption, is there unkeyed single-server PIR on every N-bit database with deterministic server-only preprocessing time and storage N times poly(lambda,log N), and worst-case online client/server time, communication and client workspace poly(lambda,log N)?
definitions:
Use security parameter lambda and negligible error as a function of lambda. The selected Ring-LWE family has power-of-two dimension d, ring R_d=Z_q[X]/(X^d+1), q=2^{ceil(sqrt(d))}, and independent integer error coefficients with probability proportional to exp(-pi e^2/d^2), reduced modulo q. For any polynomial number of samples, (a_i,a_i s+e_i), with common uniform s and independent uniform a_i in R_d, must be indistinguishable from independent uniform pairs to nonuniform polynomial-size classical adversaries as d grows. This explicit subexponential-modulus family is an editorial parameter choice. It imposes no circular-security or evasive assumption. Algorithms may choose d polynomial in lambda+log N.

The database D is any N-bit string. Prep(1^lambda,D) deterministically creates a static server data structure without communicating with a client or generating secret client keys. A fresh client given only lambda,N and index i generates a query and short temporary state. The server answers using random access to its data structure, and the client recovers D_i from the answer and its state. There is no database-dependent advice, offline download or pre-established shared secret at the client. Correctness is at least one minus negligible for every D and i.

Privacy requires indistinguishability of the server’s entire view for any two adaptively chosen index sequences of equal polynomial length, with fresh client randomness for each query. The server may know D and the complete preprocessed structure; its memory-access pattern and random coins are part of its view. Security is against polynomial-size adversaries for every N polynomially bounded in lambda, while the efficiency formulas are required for all lambda,N. The client need not hide the number of queries, and database confidentiality and malicious-server answer correctness are not required.

Costs use a bit-cost random-access machine: a memory access to an O(log(N+lambda+2))-bit word costs that many bit operations; arithmetic is charged for its actual bit complexity. Every stored bit and transmitted bit counts. There must be one polynomial p with preprocessing time and stored bits at most N p(lambda,log(N+2)), and worst-case time, communication and workspace per query at most p(lambda,log(N+2)). Preprocessing is independent of the eventual client and query sequence; no amortized online bound is substituted.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction and proofs of the specified preprocessing, online costs, correctness and privacy from the stated Ring-LWE assumption, or refute this precise variant. An N^{1+epsilon} bound for every fixed epsilon is not a quasilinear bound, and client-specific preprocessing does not qualify.
context: Lin, Mook and Wichs introduce a Ring-LWE-based unkeyed scheme whose preprocessing is performed deterministically by the server. Its published overhead remains a fixed positive power above linear.
why: The question asks whether privacy-preserving database access can have almost optimal preparation as well as fast queries.

import_provenance.original_title: Doubly efficient PIR with quasilinear server preprocessing
import_provenance.original_statement: Can single-server private information retrieval achieve N·polylog N server preprocessing time and storage together with polylog N online query time and communication under standard assumptions such as Ring LWE? The server preprocesses the public N-bit database by itself, and clients retain only poly(λ,log N) state.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial tightening of their N^{1+ε} preprocessing/storage guarantee for every fixed ε>0; their polylogarithmic online query complexity is already achieved. Client-specific preprocessing or extra noncolluding servers changes the problem.

context_blocks.text: Lin, Mook and Wichs introduce a Ring-LWE-based unkeyed scheme whose preprocessing is performed deterministically by the server. Its published overhead remains a fixed positive power above linear.

sentences: A server preprocesses a public database without involving a client.
Fresh clients retrieve individual bits without revealing their indices.
Preprocessing and storage must be quasilinear after separating security factors.
All online costs and client workspace must be polylogarithmic in database size.
The specified Ring-LWE variant and unkeyed setup exclude client-preprocessing shortcuts.
